subject.title: [Feature]: Harden Control UI Lit lifecycle boundaries

question: Should this Control UI Lit lifecycle hardening land as one coordinated modernization slice, or be split into smaller PRs by lifecycle seam?
rationale: Source evidence supports the problem, but the protected label and broad UI surface require maintainer intent on scope, sequencing, and proof before automation should implement it.

options.title: Split by lifecycle seam
options.body: Create separate reviewable PRs for shared host/i18n behavior, external-source subscriptions, router pending/not-found state, and chat post-render/persistence teardown.

options.title: Land one coordinated slice
options.body: Allow one larger refactor if the owner wants a single architectural change and it includes broad Control UI regression and browser proof.

options.title: Narrow to proven bugs only
options.body: Defer shared abstractions and only fix individual lifecycle races when each has a focused source or live reproduction.

recommendation.title: Split by lifecycle seam
recommendation.body: Create separate reviewable PRs for shared host/i18n behavior, external-source subscriptions, router pending/not-found state, and chat post-render/persistence teardown.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and merged PR metadata make `steipete` the strongest available routing candidate for the implicated Control UI files.
